body.statement: Can the multiscale Gaussian-prior handle prove \(L_G(C_n)\gtrsim d_n\) for every interval honest over \(\mathcal G_n\)? Success requires Gaussian-branch projected mixtures with bounded chi-square distance and \(\theta_0\)-separation \(c\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}\) whenever \(\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}\gg n^{-1/2}\), without a logarithmic restriction on the radii.
body.justification: It isolates the precise criterion for upgrading \(d_n^-\) to \(d_n\).
body.gap: The published Gaussian lower experiment retains \(\Lambda_n\), and no cited result removes it on this class.
body.consumer: A positive answer closes the only logarithmic gap in the Gaussian coordinate.

obligation.what_is_open: Construct, for unrestricted slowly varying treatment-nuisance radii, two Gaussian-branch projected mixtures with uniformly bounded chi-square distance and treatment-effect separation at the unattenuated nuisance-product scale, or prove that no such construction exists.
obligation.obstruction: The cited moment-matching construction uses a degree equal in order to the logarithm of sample size divided by the logarithm of the inverse treatment-nuisance radius. Its dual approximation separation is the inverse cube of that degree and therefore produces exactly the frozen logarithmic attenuation. The frozen core contains neither a sharper Gaussian dual approximation bound nor an upper experiment showing that this logarithm is necessary.
obligation.attempted: Rescale and truncate the published nuisance radii, take the construction at three times the fold size, and optimize its moment-matching degree subject to bounded product chi-square distance. This recovers the certified attenuated scale and the full rate for polynomially small treatment-nuisance radii, but the inverse-cube degree loss persists for slowly varying radii. Declaring a negative answer would require a dual optimality or counterexample result not present in the frozen primitives.
obligation.partial_result:
The available handle closes the full Gaussian rate in the polynomial treatment-nuisance regime.  Indeed, if \(\varepsilon_{g,n}=0\), then \(\Lambda_n=1\).  If instead there is a fixed \(\beta>0\) such that \(0<\varepsilon_{g,n}\le n^{-\beta}\) eventually, then
\[
 \frac{1\vee\log(1/\varepsilon_{g,n})}{\log(en)}
 \ge \frac{\beta\log n}{1+\log n}
 \ge \frac{\beta}{2}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Hence
\[
 \Lambda_n\ge\min\{1,(\beta/2)^3\},qquad
 d_n^-\ge c_\beta d_n,
\]
and the Gaussian-coordinate theorem gives \(L_G(C_n)\gtrsim_\beta d_n\) in this subregime.  For slowly varying radii such as \(\varepsilon_{g,n}=(\log n)^{-a}\), the same construction retains the factor \(\Lambda_n\asymp(\log\log n/\log n)^3\) whenever the nuisance product dominates the parametric term; no conclusion in the frozen core upgrades this to a constant factor.
